title: [25/8/2024] Proportion of population aged 65 and over
prompt: The bar chart below shows the proportion of the population aged 65 and over of three countries in 1980 and 2000 and prediction in 2030. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentages of elderly population aged 65 and above in three countries, namely Canada, Germany and the UK, in 1980 and 2000, along with projections for 2030.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three nations experienced rising proportions of elderly population between 1980 and 2000, and this trend is expected to continue until 2030. Additionally, Germany recorded the highest percentage throughout the first 20-year period and is forecast to remain in this leading position by 2030.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at Germany's figures in detail, this country started with 15% of its population being 65 and older in 1980. The proportion then rose substantially to 20% by 2000, and this upward trend is forecast to continue, reaching 25% by 2030, marking the highest level among the three countries.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining countries, in 1980, Canada recorded the lowest percentage at 10%, while the UK's figure was notably higher at 14%. The Canadian elderly population then increased steadily to 15% in 2000 and is projected to rise significantly to 22% by 2030. Similarly, the UK saw its proportion grow to 15% in 2000, though its expected increase is more modest, reaching only 19% by the end of the period.
